### Problem

The organisation now has repositories that are plugins for coding agents, not WordPress plugins: DiluxOne/dilux-agentic-workflow (DAW, one plugin wired into Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Gemini and OpenCode) and DiluxOne/diluxone-mermaid (a skill and its scripts), plus the catalog that lists them, DiluxOne/diluxone-plugins. None of them is of a kind (`repos.yml`: `kinds: []`), so the organisation's flow does not reach them: DAW calls none of the organisation's workflows, so an issue opened there gets no triage, no board and no autopilot (DiluxOne/dilux-agentic-workflow#53 has had no label nor answer since 2026-10-09, and its fix waits on an acceptance nobody can give through the flow), and `repos.yml` keeps DAW out of the merge queue as "another maintainer's repository and flow". DAW also publishes itself through a marketplace of its own (`dilux`, plugin `ddw`), beside the organisation's catalog (`diluxone`), so a person has two places to install from, and the catalog only speaks to Claude Code. Its name still says DDW in the plugin, its rules and its docs, though the repository is DAW. And `diluxone-plugins` reads as the WordPress plugins in an organisation where most repositories are WordPress plugins.

### Scope

- Carries out DiluxOne/.github#552 in this repository, accepted with it (the delegated lane).
- A new kind, `ai-agent-plugin`, in `kinds/ai-agent-plugin/`: its review profile and rules (hooks and shell commands a plugin installs, what it asks the agent to run, no credentials, the manifests of every tool it declares), its `pre-pr` (what the repository's own checks are: for DAW its `verify`, `mutations` and `behavioral` suites), its `detect`, its `autopilot` lines (the changelog and the manifests of every tool kept in step) and its `release` (a GitHub release, and the catalog's entry brought up to that version).
- The manifests per tool: the kind says which tools have a catalog (Claude Code's `marketplace.json`, and Codex, Cursor and Copilot where their documentation shows one, checked against it before it is written) and which install by instructions (Gemini, OpenCode), and checks that a plugin's manifests, for every tool it declares, agree on its name, version and description. This holds for every repository of the kind, not only DAW.
- The catalog: `diluxone-plugins` is renamed `diluxone-plugins-ai`; it lists every plugin of the kind, per tool, from each plugin's own repository (`source: github`), and its README says how to install from each tool and that whoever added the old one removes it and adds it again.
- Adopting the three repositories: `repos.yml` (kind, merge queue, `pre-pr`, `repro`), their callers of the organisation's workflows (`scripts/sync-repos.py callers`), labels, rulesets and the Project, as `docs/adopting.md` says.
- DAW, as its part: DDW becomes DAW everywhere at once (the plugin's name, `ddw/` paths, `docs/ddw/`, skills, the state file, hooks, install script and docs), with a migration for a project that already has DDW's files; its own `dilux` marketplace is removed and it is published in `diluxone-plugins-ai` for every tool it supports. No second marketplace is kept.
- diluxone-mermaid, as its part: its manifests for the tools it can support, and its entry in the catalog per tool.

### Out of scope

- DAW's OpenSpec bridge and its `autonomous` mode (DiluxOne/dilux-agentic-workflow#57): a maintainer decides them later.
- Changes to DAW's method: its ticket classifications, its phases and gates.
- The fixes already reported in DAW (#53, and the ones taken from #57): each goes through the flow on its own once the repository is adopted.
- A WordPress plugin catalog: those are published on wordpress.org.

### Acceptance criteria

- C1: Given `kinds/ai-agent-plugin/`, when the packs' checks run, then the pack is valid and `kinds/README.md` lists it with what it is for.
- C2: Given a repository of the kind whose manifests for two tools disagree on the plugin's name or version, when its pull request is checked, then the check fails and names the two files.
- C3: Given DiluxOne/dilux-agentic-workflow, when an issue is opened there, then the organisation's triage labels it and, once accepted, the autopilot starts on it.
- C4: Given DAW's `make pre-pr`, when it runs, then it runs the same suites as its pull request and its merge queue, and stops at the first failure.
- C5: Given the catalog `diluxone-plugins-ai`, when a person adds it in Claude Code, then `diluxone-mermaid` and DAW both install from it, each from its own repository.
- C6: Given DAW's default branch after its part, when it is searched for `ddw` and `DDW`, then nothing is found but the migration that reads a project's old files and its changelog's history.
- C7: Given a project that already has DDW's files, when DAW's migration runs, then the project works under DAW with its state and its gates kept.
- C8: Given DAW's repository after its part, when it is listed, then it has no marketplace of its own, and its README installs it from `diluxone-plugins-ai`.
- C9: Given the daily drift check, when it runs, then none of the three repositories is listed as out of step.

### Criticality

Normal
